clubParas: This is the LGW02 with the volume turned down. Same forged body, same grind, same behavior out of the same lies — the only thing that changed is what it looks like at address.

Blacked-out finish with gold on the clover and the loft stamp, and nothing else. At address it disappears against the grass, which some golfers find easier to aim and others find they miss the gold entirely.
It is the full six-loft lineup, unlike the gold V2, which stops at three.
Right hand today. Left hand is on the way, so if that is what you need it is worth waiting rather than settling for the gold.

paras: Gold clubs get comments. That is fine until it is not, and there is a kind of golfer who would rather the club said nothing at all.
This is that club. It still has gold on it — on the clover, on the number — but you have to be standing over it to find any.

helpLoft.headline: Start with the wedge you already carry
helpLoft.sub: Wedges work in gaps. Four to six degrees between clubs keeps your distances even and stops two wedges going the same yardage. The Black comes in all six lofts, so a full ladder is available in this finish.

_01: THE 01, BLACK. Same club as the gold on the LGW01 platform (v1.8's platform note), K grind, six lofts. $109 rather than $99 because the blacked-out finish is a real extra process — the one price difference in the wedge line that stands for something (Cole 2026-07-31).
_signoff:
GRIND COPY — read before editing.
1. Our letter names are VOKEY'S (Cole, 2026-07-31). K = the full sole with camber, the most forgiving. S = the narrower sole with heel and trailing-edge relief, for a square face and a neutral attack. S is NOT the open-the-face versatility grind; that is Vokey's M, which we do not make. An early draft had that wrong.
2. THE SPEC SHEET IS TRUE (Cole, 2026-07-31). Our S measures equal or more bounce than our K at every shared loft — 52 K=8 S=10, 56 K=12 S=12, 60 K=10 S=12 — which looks backwards for Vokey letters until you separate MEASURED bounce from EFFECTIVE bounce. A narrow sole with relief ground off the heel and trailing edge presents less of itself to the turf, so it can carry more measured bounce and still play lower than a full cambered sole. That is standard wedge design, not a Lucky-specific claim, and it is the honest reconciliation of the two facts. The page now says it out loud rather than leaving a customer to think the table is a typo.
3. Every number in `facts` is the manufacturer sheet. The sole descriptions are the standard meaning of the letters. The measured-vs-effective explanation is general equipment design.

grinds.headline: One sole, and it is the forgiving one.
grinds.sub: Grind is the shape of the sole — the part of the club that meets the turf. The Black is built on the K grind, the fuller sole. If you want the narrower S, it is on the Gold.

options.name: The forgiving one
options.forWho: Soft turf, and a real divot
paras: K grind is the fuller sole, with camber through it, so the club skids across the ground instead of catching in it. More of the sole is in contact with the turf, which is what makes it the forgiving one out of soft lies and out of sand.

The bounce steps with the loft rather than sitting flat: 8° on the 50 and the 52, where you are hitting full shots and do not want the sole in the way; 12° on the 54 and the 56, which are the ones you take into a bunker; 10° on the 58 and the 60.

facts.v: 8° at 50 and 52 · 12° at 54 and 56 · 10° at 58 and 60

grinds.short: Short version: K for soft turf and a real divot. The S grind, for firm turf and tight lies, is on the 01 Gold.
